mentions.name: tina
mentions.description: An open-source high-throughput concurrency framework that bridges Erlang-style concurrency with native performance, running without a VM or garbage collector. It aims to let developers program concurrent systems while avoiding the gotchas of common primitives such as callbacks and promise chains.
mentions.problem: Today's concurrency primitives (e.g. callbacks/promise hell) have gotchas that make programming concurrent systems difficult.
mentions.source_excerpt: So I recently open sourced it (https://github.com/pmbanugo/tina). It's a high-throughput concurrency framework that bridges the Erlang-style concurrency with native performance (no VM, no GC).
